description.narrative: Currently, Sierra Leone has 43 confirmed cases of COVID-19. While the Government acted quickly in order to prevent and deter the spread, the amount of cases quickly escalated over a period of just two weeks. As one of the poorest countries in the world, the further spread of COVID-19 has the capacity to destroy the fragile economic system and counteract the progress that has been made since Ebola. Lessons learnt from Ebola have shown that key interventions in preventing the spread are awareness-raising and social mobilization, especially in rural areas. While Freetown has so far been the epicenter of the outbreak, it is quickly spreading to other towns and communities. With limited access to information, rumors and false information has the capacity to spread rapidly in rural areas. If it continues to spread further, the virus is likely to have the most devastating impact in rural communities. Therefore, CAFOD plans to support Inter-Religious Council of Sierra Leone to prepare rural communities to better prevent and respond to the spread of COVID-19 through the use of local experts and religious leaders for awareness-raising, ensuring access to correct and up to date information and advocacy and awareness for health officials on data protection.
